grounded_facts: The robed figures transport the Girl in a floating cage, separating her from Sam.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Sam responds to Mr. Kurtzman's concern about malfunctioning electronics by reassuring him that he will come in.

grounded_facts: Sam briefly believes Jill is the girl from his dream upon seeing her image on a security screen, but fails to recognize her in person when she turns away.
memories.memory_text: I briefly thought the woman on the security screen was the girl from my dream, but when I looked around, she had her back to me and I didn't recognize her in person.

memories.memory_text: I saw a prototype surveillance camera intrude on Jill during a demonstration, and when she swatted it away, it crashed into the desk, sparking and malfunctioning.

memories.memory_text: I saw Jill trying to report a wrongful arrest at the information desk, but the porter refused to give her the form because her receipt wasn't stamped and told her to go back to Information Adjustments.

grounded_facts: Jill approaches the Information desk to report a wrongful arrest and request a form, but is turned away due to procedural requirements.
memories.memory_text: I saw a woman at the Information desk who tried to report a wrongful arrest and ask for a form, but she was turned away because of the procedures.

grounded_facts: A salesman demonstrates a new radio-controlled surveillance camera to a group of technicians, using live footage from the lobby.
memories.memory_text: I passed a group of technicians watching a demonstration of a new radio-controlled surveillance camera that was showing live footage from the lobby.

grounded_facts: Kurtzman expresses relief that the error was not their fault, showing dependence on Sam's expertise.
memories.memory_text: I fixed the error at the console while Kurtzman watched, and when he worried it was our mistake, I told him it wasn't—I traced it to Information Retrieval, and he actually said he was relieved, like he couldn't handle me moving up.

grounded_facts: Sam repeatedly insists he would refuse a promotion, indicating discomfort with upward mobility.
memories.memory_text: I told Kurtzman again that I'd turn down any promotion—he asked if I really meant it, and I said yes, really—because I mean it, I don't want any of that.

memories.memory_text: I was working at the console in Mr. Kurtzman's office, trying to fix a system error, and I realized it wasn't the machine—it was a mismatch in the personnel code numbers. I found that the system confused Archibald Buttle with Archibald Tuttle, wrongly debiting Buttle instead of Tuttle, and I made sure to point out it wasn't our mistake when Kurtzman handed me the printout.

grounded_facts: Upon learning of his promotion, Sam angrily attributes it to his mother's manipulation.

memories.memory_text: I was handed a transfer notice to Information Retrieval at Security Level 3, and when Kurtzman suggested my mother was pulling strings again, I thought of her and just called her a bitch—I knew it was her doing, forcing me into a move I never wanted.

grounded_facts: Sam voices anger and frustration toward his mother for pushing him to seek promotion, asserting he is content in his current position.
memories.memory_text: I told my mother I was angry about her interference and that I don't want promotion—I'm happy in my current job.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Lowry insists that Sam lacks ambition and needs her intervention to advance, citing Jack Lint as a cautionary example.
memories.memory_text: My mother told me I lack ambition and need her help to get ahead, using Jack Lint as an example of someone who succeeded through drive, not intelligence.

grounded_facts: The doctor tells Sam to wait in reception, implying his presence is disruptive to the patient.
memories.memory_text: I was told to wait in reception because my presence was giving my mother wrinkles.

grounded_facts: The doctor uses colored markers and cellophane to simulate a facelift on Mrs. Lowry, illustrating the expected surgical outcome.
memories.memory_text: I watched the doctor use colored markers on my mother's face to show how the facelift would smooth out her wrinkles and lift the skin into her hairline, but then he told me to wait in reception because I was giving her wrinkles.

grounded_facts: The doctor presents the simulated facelift result with triumph, claiming Mrs. Lowry already appears twice as beautiful.
memories.memory_text: I saw the doctor place cellophane over my mother's face and stick it down, and he said triumphantly that she already looked twice as beautiful.

grounded_facts: A scheduled appointment in which Dr. Jaffe consults with Mrs. Lowry about an upcoming facelift procedure, including a visual simulation of results.
memories.memory_text: I was in the room when Dr. Jaffe showed my mother a simulation of her facelift results, pulling at her cheeks and promising to make her twenty years younger.

grounded_facts: Mother insists Sam will like working under Mr. Helpmann at Information Retrieval, promoting a career path he does not want.
memories.memory_text: My mother told me I'd like working under Mr. Helpmann at Information Retrieval, saying he was close to my father and would take me under his wing, and that the promotion was very exclusive.

grounded_facts: Mother's handbag triggers a security alarm due to an executive toy inside, which is inspected and returned.
memories.memory_text: I was going through security with my mother when her handbag set off the alarm because of an executive toy inside, which they inspected and then returned to her.

grounded_facts: Spiro initially blocks Sam's entry and shows disdain for his appearance, only changing attitude when reminded of his relation to Mother.
memories.memory_text: I saw the maitre d' block me at first and show clear disdain for how I looked, but he changed his attitude immediately when my mother reminded him we were meeting Mrs. Terrain.

grounded_facts: Sam and his mother are admitted into the restaurant by the maitre d' and led to Mrs. Terrain's table.
memories.memory_text: I remember the maitre d' eventually leading my mother and me across the restaurant to Mrs. Terrain's table, with a string quartet playing as we walked.

grounded_facts: A formal lunch gathering at a high-end restaurant involving Sam, his mother, Mrs. Terrain, and Shirley.
memories.memory_text: I was part of a formal lunch at a high-end restaurant with my mother, Mrs. Terrain, and her daughter Shirley, where we were all seated together at their table.

grounded_facts: Mrs. Terrain questions when Sam will 'do something about these terrorists' after the explosion, implying responsibility.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mrs. Terrain to do something about the terrorists right after the explosion, but I couldn't believe she expected me to handle that during my lunch hour.

grounded_facts: After Sam's outburst, Shirley expresses violent support against 'murderous bastards', aligning with perceived authority.
memories.memory_text: I saw Shirley shout something about 'fucking murderous bastards' after my outburst, though I'm not sure who she meant.

grounded_facts: Shirley timidly offers salt and later pepper to Sam, attempting minor social engagement.
memories.memory_text: I remember Shirley timidly offering me salt and then pepper, trying to make small talk during the meal.

grounded_facts: A massive explosion blasts a hole in the wall leading to the kitchen, causing chaos, injuries, and emergency response.
memories.memory_text: I saw the massive explosion that blew a hole in the wall to the kitchen, and I watched as the staff scrambled to block off the view of the victims.

grounded_facts: Sam publicly refuses the promotion to Information Retrieval that his mother announced, expressing anger and throwing away the notification.
memories.memory_text: I refused the promotion to Information Retrieval right there, shouting that I wasn't going, telling my mother where she could stick her interference, and later saying I didn't want promotion or anything at all.

grounded_facts: Sam emphatically denies having any dreams, not even in the form of nighttime visions, rejecting an implied expectation or assumption.
memories.memory_text: I made it clear that I don't want promotion, I don't want dessert, and I don't want anything—not even dreams.

grounded_facts: Sam decides to leave the restaurant before dessert, rejecting both food and social expectations.
memories.memory_text: I decided to leave the table early because I needed to get back, and I didn't want to stay for dessert or any of the expectations that came with it.

grounded_facts: Sam tells the girl she is now safe and unreachable by their pursuers.
memories.memory_text: I told the girl I was taking her to a safe place where they could never get at us, and I reassured her there was no way their pursuers could approach without being seen, so she was safe now.

grounded_facts: The girl cries out for Sam to save her as the sky collapses.
memories.memory_text: I heard the girl crying out for me to save her as the sky collapsed around us.

memories.memory_text: I got up and checked the thermostat, and it read 99 degrees; I tried to adjust it, but it was stuck and wouldn't change no matter how much I fiddled with it.

grounded_facts: Sam forcibly opens the sealed window using a knife to escape the heat, only to be met with toxic smog.
memories.memory_text: I tried to open the sealed window to get some fresh air because the heat was unbearable, so I used a knife to unscrew it; I swung it open and took a deep breath, but immediately I was hit by a wave of toxic smog that made me gag and cough—I had to shut it fast and tighten the screws again.

memories.memory_text: I called Central Services from my kitchen, trying to get help for my broken air conditioning, and even asked for a heating engineer, but the automated system rejected my request and I had to slam the phone down in frustration.

grounded_facts: Sam sits in front of the open refrigerator with a chair wedged in the door to stay cool, indicating deteriorating living conditions.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Sam sits in front of the open refrigerator with a chair wedged in the door to stay cool, indicating deteriorating living conditions.

grounded_facts: While falling asleep in front of the refrigerator, Sam knocks over a jar of pickled onions, spilling them.
memories.memory_text: I remember that While falling asleep in front of the refrigerator, Sam knocks over a jar of pickled onions, spilling them.

grounded_facts: Sam climbs inside a giant eyeball to escape the intergalactic maelstrom, discovering a hidden hatch and entering its interior space.
memories.memory_text: I climbed inside a giant eyeball to escape the intergalactic maelstrom, and I forced open a hidden hatch to get through.

grounded_facts: Sam emerges from the eyeball hatch into a vast vertical structure composed of filing drawers, realizing he is high above a misty abyss.
memories.memory_text: I emerged from the hatch into a vast vertical structure of filing drawers, and I realized I was high above a misty abyss.

grounded_facts: The Jolly Gent greets Sam by name and asserts that they know everything about him.
memories.memory_text: I remember the man calling me by name, saying 'Ah ha ... there you are, Sam,' and telling me they know everything about me here in the Storeroom of Knowledge.

grounded_facts: A vast, institutional space composed of filing cabinets where all knowledge and experiences are stored and managed by attendants.
memories.memory_text: I was told that this place is the Storeroom of Knowledge, where every bit of knowledge, wisdom, learning, and experience is neatly filed away.

grounded_facts: The Jolly Gent implies that assistance will be granted if Sam helps them in return.
memories.memory_text: I was told that they would help me only if I helped them in return, and that the Forces of Darkness had won the day but tomorrow was another one.

memories.memory_text: I remember that The Jolly Gent gives Sam the Sword of Truth, Helmet of Justice, and a cape, outfitting him for a mission to save the day.

memories.memory_text: I remember that The Jolly Gent hands Sam the Sword of Truth, Helmet of Justice, and a cape, completing his transformation into a hero.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Sam lies down in a filing drawer which is then closed, experiencing a sudden vision of a samurai warrior instead of the Jolly Gent.

memories.memory_text: I remember that The Jolly Gent pushes Sam into the drawer, triggering Sam's claustrophobia and a disturbing vision.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Sam realizes the threatening voice is both on the phone and in the room, leading him to turn and see Tuttle pointing a gun at him.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Tuttle uses a phone call and visible firearm to force Sam into compliance upon entry.

memories.memory_text: I was told by Tuttle that he hates Central Services' excessive paperwork and that he works outside the system because he came into the job for adventure, not forms.

grounded_facts: Tuttle identifies a charred gadget as the source of the malfunction and replaces it with an improvised bypass device.
memories.memory_text: I saw Tuttle hold up a small charred gadget and say he could bypass the problem with one of his own devices, fixing my air-conditioning illegally while I stood there with his gun pointed at me.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Spoor and Dowser arrive to inspect Sam's air-conditioning, suspecting tampering, but are repelled by procedural manipulation.

memories.memory_text: I stood my ground at the door and asked Spoor and Dowser if they had a Form 27B/6, knowing they couldn't enter without it, and I made sure to emphasize my strict adherence to procedure before ushering them out.

grounded_facts: Tuttle acknowledges Sam's quick thinking in preventing discovery by inspectors.
memories.memory_text: I remember Tuttle telling me, 'Thanks, Lowry, you're a good man in a tight corner,' after I helped him avoid the inspectors.

grounded_facts: Tuttle disarms, introduces himself as a rogue heating engineer, and begins repairing Sam's air-conditioning system illegally.
memories.memory_text: I saw Tuttle disarm and introduce himself as a rogue heating engineer before starting to fix my air-conditioning system illegally.

grounded_facts: An unsanctioned visit by Tuttle to repair Sam's air-conditioning system, conducted under threat of discovery by Central Services.
memories.memory_text: I remember that An unsanctioned visit by Tuttle to repair Sam's air-conditioning system, conducted under threat of discovery by Central Services.

grounded_facts: After finishing the repair, Tuttle evades detection by swinging across a void to a neighboring building using a pre-arranged rope.
memories.memory_text: I saw Tuttle slip away down the balcony and then swing across the void to the next building using a rope he'd set up beforehand.

grounded_facts: The clerk next to Sam remarks that Kurtzman seems suspicious, possibly indicating tension or unusual office dynamics.
memories.memory_text: I was told by the clerk next to me that Kurtzman seems suspicious.

grounded_facts: Sam asks his neighbour what they are working on for the day, showing routine office communication.
memories.memory_text: I asked my neighbour what we were working on for the day.

grounded_facts: Mr. Kurtzman calls Mr. Lowry into his office and closes the door, marking a shift in the scene and indicating a private interaction.
Kurtzman publicly calls Lowry into his office, asserting authority and initiating a private encounter.
memories.memory_text: I was in the office when Mr. Kurtzman called me into his room and closed the door, which felt like a shift from public to private — a moment where his authority was clear and our interaction became personal.

grounded_facts: Kurtzman receives a refund cheque for Buttle, which causes immediate concern due to its problematic implications.
memories.memory_text: I walked into Kurtzman's office and he immediately panicked, shoving a cheque at me and saying it was a refund for Buttle, which was terrible trouble because someone would get blamed when they found it.

grounded_facts: Sam discovers through system checks that Buttle is dead, eliminating the possibility of returning the cheque through official channels.
memories.memory_text: I saw the system records and confirmed he is dead, so I knew we couldn't return the cheque through official channels.

grounded_facts: Sam identifies Mrs. Veronica Buttle as Buttle's next of kin, opening a new path to resolve the cheque issue.
memories.memory_text: I identified Mrs. Veronica Buttle as the next of kin and said, 'There we go. Mrs. Veronica Buttle,' knowing she was the one to receive the cheque.

grounded_facts: The attempt to deposit the cheque into Mrs. Buttle's bank account fails because she has no account.
memories.memory_text: I saw that Mrs. Buttle doesn't have a bank account, so I couldn't deposit the cheque electronically.

grounded_facts: Sam suggests personally delivering the cheque to Mrs. Buttle as a last resort.
Sam decides to personally deliver the cheque to Mrs. Buttle and instruct her to cash it locally.
memories.memory_text: I suggested driving out to Mrs. Buttle to give her the cheque and tell her to sign it and cash it at the corner sweet shop, and I told her I'd handle it personally and asked for the address.

grounded_facts: An urgent, informal meeting between Sam and Kurtzman in Kurtzman's office to resolve the issue of a problematic refund cheque.
memories.memory_text: I sat down and handled the refund cheque myself, authorizing it and preparing the receipts for Kurtzman to sign, then I secured the cheque and documents in a cannister and sent them off through the vacuum tube to resolve the issue.

grounded_facts: Sam signs Kurtzman's name on the cheque and receipts after Kurtzman fails due to physical distress, taking full responsibility for the action.
Sam takes the pen from Kurtzman and signs the documents on his behalf when Kurtzman is unable to do so.
memories.memory_text: I took the pen from Kurtzman and signed the cheque and receipts myself when he couldn't do it because he thought he'd broken a bone, and I made sure everything was sent off properly.

grounded_facts: Sam turns off the radio to stop listening to the news about a terrorist bombing.
memories.memory_text: I turned off the radio while driving through the tunnel to stop hearing the news about the terrorist bombing.

grounded_facts: Sam attempts to ask a group of children for help, but is immediately told to leave.
Sam politely asks a child for help but is immediately told to leave.
memories.memory_text: I politely asked a child for help, but they immediately told me to eff off, so I backed away, uncomfortable and rejected, realizing I wasn't welcome here.

grounded_facts: Sam arrives at the run-down Buttle Flats housing tower in his car, stepping into a hostile and deteriorating environment.
Sam's arrival and entry into the Buttle Flats housing complex, marked by environmental decay and social tension.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the run-down Buttle Flats housing tower in my car, stepping out into a decaying environment where locals watched me coldly, and I could feel their hostility as I moved toward the building while one of the kids approached my car with something in hand.

grounded_facts: After Sam enters the building, some of the children begin tampering with his parked car, suggesting potential vandalism.
memories.memory_text: I saw one of the kids approaching my car with a can of something after I entered the building, and another was fiddling with a box of matches, so I feared they might vandalize it.

grounded_facts: Sam tries to use the lift in the apartment block, but it malfunctions, sparking and jamming open to reveal a garbage-filled interior.
memories.memory_text: I tried to use the lift by pressing the button, but it didn't respond, so I pulled the doors apart—they jammed open with a gap, shuddering and sparking, and inside I saw it was filled with garbage, junk, old furniture, and dead cats.

grounded_facts: After failing to use the broken lift, Sam resigns himself to using the stairs.
memories.memory_text: I resigned myself to using the stairs after the lift failed and turned away from it.

grounded_facts: After receiving no response, Sam pushes the door open slightly and enters the hall with about two-thirds of his body.
memories.memory_text: I pushed the door open a bit more and put about two-thirds of my body into the hall after getting no response.

grounded_facts: Sam arrives at apartment 37, attempting to knock on the door but finding it already cracked open.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at apartment 37 and went to knock on the door, but I noticed it was already cracked open, so I knocked feebly on the frame and pushed it a bit more to peer inside.

grounded_facts: Sam calls out to Mrs Buttle twice, receiving no response.
memories.memory_text: I called out to Mrs Buttle twice—first just her name, then 'Uh, Mrs Buttle?' and finally 'Mrs Buttle...'—but I didn't get any response.

grounded_facts: Sam Lowry delivers a refund cheque to Mrs Buttle as an unorthodox payment from the Ministry of Information, explaining that Mr Buttle was overcharged.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Sam Lowry delivers a refund cheque to Mrs Buttle as an unorthodox payment from the Ministry of Information, explaining that Mr Buttle was overcharged.

grounded_facts: Mrs Buttle tears up the cheque and receipts Sam offers and throws them in his face, expressing her anger and grief.
memories.memory_text: I offered Mrs Buttle the cheque and receipts, but she tore them up and threw them in my face, screaming her anger at me.

grounded_facts: The young boy launches himself at Sam with ferocity, kicking and pulling his hair, causing Sam to fall and become injured.
memories.memory_text: I saw the boy in the doorway and then he launched at me with ferocity, kicking and pulling my hair until I fell to the ground, hurting and dazed.

grounded_facts: Mrs Buttle confronts Sam with the realization that her husband is dead, shifting the emotional tone of the interaction from bureaucratic to tragic.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Mrs Buttle confronts Sam with the realization that her husband is dead, shifting the emotional tone of the interaction from bureaucratic to tragic.

grounded_facts: Sam Lowry visits the Buttle family to deliver a refund cheque in person due to administrative difficulties, marking an informal and emotionally charged encounter.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Sam Lowry visits the Buttle family to deliver a refund cheque in person due to administrative difficulties, marking an informal and emotionally charged encounter.

grounded_facts: In Sam's hallucinated vision, Jill appears in the mirror and asks if Sam is alright, then turns to ask Mrs Buttle the same.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jill's face in a broken piece of mirror on the floor, looking at me just like she did in my dreams, and she asked if I was alright before turning to ask Mrs Buttle the same.

grounded_facts: After the failed vision of Jill, Sam rushes out of the Buttle apartment in a dazed state, attempting to pursue the apparition.
memories.memory_text: After the vision faded, I stood up dazed, looked at the empty hole in the ceiling, shouted for her to come back, and then I rushed out of the apartment trying to follow her.

grounded_facts: Sam moves toward the stairs after checking both directions in the corridor.
memories.memory_text: I looked both ways in the corridor and then moved toward the stairs.

grounded_facts: Sam is unable to determine the correct door because he forgot to count the doors downstairs.
memories.memory_text: I ran down the corridor but realized I hadn't counted the doors downstairs, so I couldn't tell which one was the right door to knock on.

grounded_facts: Sam rings the doorbell of a door he hopes is correct, but the bell does not work.
memories.memory_text: I rang the doorbell, hoping it was the right door, but the bell didn't work.

grounded_facts: Sam attempts to obtain information or access by mentioning the girl with fair hair, but is met with hostility and the door is shut.
memories.memory_text: I tried to get information by mentioning the girl with fair hair, but they reacted with hostility and shut the door on me.

grounded_facts: After banging on the door, it opens slightly and a malevolent eye observes Sam, who then identifies the girl he is seeking; the door is immediately shut.
memories.memory_text: I banged on the door and it opened slightly, revealing a malevolent eye; I said 'girl, fair hair' and the door shut immediately.

grounded_facts: After being rejected, Sam rushes to the next door in the corridor to continue his search.
memories.memory_text: I rushed to the next door in the corridor after being rejected, still unsure which room I was looking for because I hadn't counted the doors downstairs.

grounded_facts: Sam enters Jill's flat and observes the hole in the floor and the derelict state of the place, indicating recent destruction or abandonment.
memories.memory_text: I burst into Jill's flat and saw the hole in the floor, realizing how derelict and damaged the place had become.

grounded_facts: An explosion occurs, drawing Sam's attention; he sees his car on fire outside the flat.
memories.memory_text: I heard an explosion and looked out the window to see my car on fire, understanding immediately that I was in danger.

grounded_facts: Sam rushes down the stairs, indicating urgency or haste in movement.
memories.memory_text: I rushed down the stairs, moving as fast as I could.

grounded_facts: Sam tries to smother the flames on the Messerchmidt by covering it with a mattress.
memories.memory_text: I spotted a mattress by the building and grabbed it to throw over the burning car, trying to smother the flames.

grounded_facts: Jill returns in her lorry, driving past Sam at speed.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jill suddenly come roaring around the corner in her lorry, and I realized she was driving it herself.

grounded_facts: Sam shouts to Jill, denying involvement in the fire as she drives away.
memories.memory_text: I shouted at her, 'Wait! It was nothing to do with me!' as she drove away, desperate for her to know I wasn't involved in the fire.

grounded_facts: Sam finds that all three wheels of his vehicle have been removed, rendering it immobile.
memories.memory_text: I flung myself into my three-wheeler and tried to start it, but I didn't move an inch—all three wheels had been removed.

grounded_facts: A chaotic scene at a residential block where Sam reacts to the burning car, Jill's departure, and sabotage of his vehicle.
memories.memory_text: I charged out and saw the Messerchmidt was on fire, Jill was at the wheel but then disappeared, and when I turned around, I saw the children watching me silently.

grounded_facts: Sam tells Girl Buttle to go away after failing to understand her.
memories.memory_text: I told the girl to go away because I didn't understand what she was trying to say.

grounded_facts: Girl Buttle tells Sam that Jill's full name is Jill Layton.
Girl Buttle reveals that the woman Sam knows as Jill is named Jill Layton.
memories.memory_text: I was told that the woman I know as Jill is actually named Jill Layton.

grounded_facts: Sam suddenly realizes something important about Girl Buttle and turns back to look at her.
memories.memory_text: I suddenly realized something important about Girl Buttle and turned back to look at her.

grounded_facts: Kurtzman asks Sam if he knows anything about a missing personnel transporter, possibly suspecting his involvement.
memories.memory_text: Kurtzman asked me if I knew anything about a missing personnel transporter, as if he suspected I might be involved.

grounded_facts: Kurtzman checks whether Sam completed the task of delivering Mrs. Buttle's cheque.
memories.memory_text: Kurtzman checked whether I had delivered Mrs. Buttle's cheque, and I confirmed I had, so he could forget about it.

grounded_facts: Sam accesses a computer system to retrieve personal information about Jill, but the data is blocked by a 'Classified' overprint and IRQ/3 alert, indicating restricted access due to her status as a Level 3 Suspect.
memories.memory_text: I tried to pull up Jill's personal dossier on the computer, entering her details and attempting to cancel the 'Classified' overprint, but an IRQ/3 alert blocked the information and only her two-view portrait printed out.

grounded_facts: Frustrated by the classified status of Jill's file, Sam concludes he must accept a promotion to gain the necessary clearance to investigate further.
memories.memory_text: After seeing the file was blocked, I asked Kurtzman if there was a way around the IRQ/3 restriction, and I realized I’d have to accept the promotion to get the clearance needed to find out more about Jill.

grounded_facts: Kurtzman discloses that he has already submitted the promotion paperwork on Sam's behalf, making the decision effectively irreversible without formal withdrawal.
memories.memory_text: Kurtzman told me he had already submitted the promotion paperwork for me, and when I reacted with shock, he insisted it was what I wanted, but I wasn't even sure myself.

grounded_facts: After picking up the printed image of Jill, Kurtzman grimaces and drops it with a shudder, indicating fear or unease.
memories.memory_text: I saw Kurtzman pick up the printed image of Jill and grimace before dropping it with a shudder, as if he were afraid of it.

grounded_facts: The daily office closure in the Record Clerks Pool, where staff are leaving and lights are being turned off.
memories.memory_text: I saw the office closing down around me, with lights being turned off and staff leaving, so I shut down my machine and followed Kurtzman out.

grounded_facts: Sam transforms a computer print-out of Jill into the Dream Girl by drawing long flowing hair on it.
memories.memory_text: I transformed a computer print-out of Jill by drawing long flowing hair on it, turning her into the Dream Girl.

grounded_facts: Sam is so focused on Jill's picture that he almost fails to get off the transport cage at his corridor platform.
memories.memory_text: I was so focused on Jill's picture that I almost missed getting off the transport cage at my corridor platform.

grounded_facts: After disembarking, Sam appears to be struggling with a decision as he moves toward his front door.
memories.memory_text: I was trying to make up my mind about something as I headed toward my front door.

grounded_facts: Spoor uses a recording of Sam's call to justify the emergency entry.
memories.memory_text: I heard Spoor play back my own call to Central Services, using it to justify breaking into my flat as if it were a real emergency.

grounded_facts: Spoor insists Sam sign a form to formalize the emergency service.
memories.memory_text: I reluctantly signed the 27B/6 form Spoor handed me, page after page, even though I didn’t understand it and only did so because he insisted.

grounded_facts: Dowser discovers a spare part linked to Tuttle inside the wall, implicating him in prior repairs.
memories.memory_text: I watched in alarm as Dowser burst through the wall panel and pulled out a spare part still attached to a rubber tube—Tuttle’s part—and Spoor started examining it closely.

grounded_facts: Sam signs a 27B/6 form under pressure, legitimizing the crew's entry.
memories.memory_text: I signed the form they shoved in front of me, even though I told them there was no emergency and I didn't want them in my flat.

grounded_facts: Spoor accuses Sam of using Tuttle’s parts, implying sabotage against Central Services.
After finding Tuttle's part, Spoor and Dowser confront Sam about his association with Tuttle.
memories.memory_text: Spoor confronted me, accusing me of letting Tuttle in and using his parts, and when he held up the part and shouted about sabotage, I realized they thought I was involved; then he grabbed my form-book, ripped out the page, and shoved it at me before leaving.

grounded_facts: Spoor sarcastically tells Sam to 'blow yer nose and fix it', ridiculing his situation.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Spoor to 'blow yer nose and fix it,' mocking me as if my problems were trivial.

grounded_facts: An unsolicited repair crew enters Sam's flat under emergency protocols to fix ducts, leading to confrontation and abandonment.
Spoor and Dowser enter Sam's flat under emergency procedures, initiating intrusive repairs.
memories.memory_text: I came back to my flat and found it torn apart, with Spoor directing workmen and Dowser banging inside the walls — they forced their way in under emergency protocols and left me alone in the wreckage after they finished.

grounded_facts: Spoor and Dowser abruptly terminate repairs and leave Sam's flat in ruins.
memories.memory_text: I saw Spoor and Dowser pack up their tools and leave abruptly, abandoning me in the wreckage of my flat after they tore everything apart.

grounded_facts: After the crew leaves, Sam collapses and stares at a print-out of Jill's face, which dissolves into the Dream Girl.
memories.memory_text: I collapsed onto the couch after they left, and I just stared at the print-out of Jill's face—then it slowly dissolved into the Dream Girl.

grounded_facts: Sam reaches out and embraces the Dream Girl, but she dissolves in smoke, leading to his fall.
memories.memory_text: I reached out and embraced the Dream Girl, but she dissolved into smoke, and I plummeted into a void beneath my feet.

grounded_facts: Sam uses his cape as a parachute to slow his fall after freeing it from his body during a plummet through the clouds.
memories.memory_text: I was plummeting through the clouds with my cape tangled around me, so I wrestled it free, gripped the corners, and whipped it over my head—I saw the wind catch it and slow my fall, and then the clouds thinned and I could see the ground below.

grounded_facts: The clouds thin out, allowing Sam to see the ground below him for the first time during his fall.
memories.memory_text: I saw the ground below me for the first time as the clouds suddenly thinned during my fall.

grounded_facts: Sam lands on the barren landscape using his cape-parachute, marking the beginning of his direct involvement in the scene.
memories.memory_text: I landed on the barren landscape using my cape as a parachute, feeling the impact as my feet touched the ground.

grounded_facts: Sam identifies Mrs Buttle, people from the flats, and the kids among the prisoners, establishing personal stakes.
memories.memory_text: I saw Mrs Buttle among the prisoners, along with people I recognized from the flats and the kids, and I realized they were in danger.

grounded_facts: Sam draws his sword in determination upon recognizing the prisoners, signaling resolve.
memories.memory_text: I drew my sword, feeling a surge of determination to act after seeing the people I knew being taken.

grounded_facts: A forced loading of prisoners into two giant cages suspended beneath balloons, conducted by the Forces of Darkness.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the prisoners being forced into the giant cages beneath balloons, pushed forward by the Forces of Darkness with whips and prods.

grounded_facts: The Giant Samurai Warrior emerges from the fissure and confronts Sam, then vanishes after a ritualistic gesture.
memories.memory_text: I turned to face the Giant Samurai Warrior that emerged from the fissure; I stepped toward him, but he stood still and then vanished in an instant, cutting off the light.

grounded_facts: A violent tremor causes a crack to open in the earth between Sam and the prisoners, blocking access.
memories.memory_text: I was trying to reach the prisoners when a violent tremor hit, and a crack suddenly opened in the ground between me and them, blocking my way.

grounded_facts: The first caged prisoner group ascends into the sky, escorted by the black flapping entity.
memories.memory_text: I saw the first cage of prisoners rising into the sky, escorted by the black flapping entity, so I rushed after it and grabbed a trailing rope to climb up, but the FODS severed it and I fell back down.

grounded_facts: Sam tries to board the ascending cage by grabbing a rope, but is cut down by the FOD.
memories.memory_text: I rushed after the cage and grabbed one of the trailing ropes, trying to climb up, but the FODs cut the rope and I tumbled back to the ground.

grounded_facts: Sam cuts the tethers of the second caged balloon, causing it to begin ascending.
memories.memory_text: I ran to the second cage and started cutting the tethers, and I remember the moment I severed the last rope— the cage began to rise.

grounded_facts: Mr Kurtzman, emerging from a smoking mound, grabs Sam and warns him not to proceed, claiming it's a trap.
memories.memory_text: I saw Mr Kurtzman's face emerge from a smoking mound and he grabbed me, shouting that it was a trap and 'she' was not what she seemed.

grounded_facts: Mr Kurtzman physically restrains Sam and verbally warns him that proceeding is a trap and 'she' is not what she seems.
memories.memory_text: After hearing Mr Kurtzman warn me, I kept struggling against his giant hands, kicking and straining to break free, but he held me firmly in place.

grounded_facts: Sam wakes up with his feet tangled in wiring and ducting in his devastated sitting room.
memories.memory_text: I woke up with my feet tangled in wiring and ducting, still in my devastated sitting room, and I had to untangle myself before I could even get to the door.

grounded_facts: A party hosted by Mrs. Ida Lowry to celebrate her recent cosmetic surgery, scheduled from 8:30 PM to midnight, with Conrad Helpmann as guest of honor.
memories.memory_text: I was told there's a party hosted by Mrs. Ida Lowry tonight from 8:30 PM to midnight to celebrate her recent cosmetic surgery, and Conrad Helpmann is the guest of honor.

grounded_facts: A girl in a bell-boy costume delivers a singing invitation to Sam for Ida Lowry's party.
memories.memory_text: I saw a girl in a bell-boy costume burst into my room and start performing a song and dance for me.

grounded_facts: Sam notes that the telegram is late, as the party started half an hour ago.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the telegram was late because the party had already started half an hour ago, and I said so when I saw the girl.

grounded_facts: The girl performs a singing telegram to formally invite Sam to Ida Lowry's party.
memories.memory_text: I heard the girl sing a formal invitation from Ida Lowry for her party, mentioning the time, the reason, and that Conrad Helpmann would be there.

grounded_facts: Sam awkwardly responds to the singing telegram, confirming he has received the invitation.
memories.memory_text: I awkwardly responded to the singing telegram with a hesitant 'Thanks' and later confirmed I received it by saying, 'Yes, it was ... very nice ... thank you.'

grounded_facts: After delivering the telegram, the girl asks Sam if she can use his bathroom.
memories.memory_text: After she handed me the telegram, the girl asked if she could use my bathroom, and I remember her asking me directly.

grounded_facts: Sam arrives at his mother's flat and rings the doorbell, marking his presence at the event.
memories.memory_text: I rang the doorbell at my mother's flat to let them know I had arrived.

grounded_facts: A formal gathering at Sam's mother's flat, attended by staff and guests, implied by Sam's dress and the livery of the attendant.
memories.memory_text: I noticed my own tuxedo and the livery of the attendant, and I figured there must be some kind of formal gathering going on at my mother's flat.

grounded_facts: The woman expresses pleasure at Sam's arrival and invites him in.
memories.memory_text: I heard the woman say, 'Sam, I'm so glad you came. Do come in,' and felt welcomed as she invited me inside.

grounded_facts: Sam expresses intent to speak with Mr Helpmann, indicating a proactive move in their relationship.
memories.memory_text: I told someone I wanted to talk to Mr Helpmann, making it clear I needed to speak with him directly.

grounded_facts: Sam enters his mother's flat, where a flunky begins to search him, marking his arrival at a high-society gathering.
memories.memory_text: I stepped into my mother's flat and immediately had to push away the flunky who started searching me with a metal detector.

grounded_facts: Sam's refusal of a promotion is revealed, marking a significant professional divergence.
memories.memory_text: I was told that my refusal of the promotion had surprised everyone, and that my mother thought I should see a doctor about it.

grounded_facts: Dr Jaffe drunkenly brags to Sam about his surgical success, particularly on women's bodies, repulsing Sam.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Dr Jaffe, who was clearly drunk, about his surgical work, especially on women's bodies, and I found his bragging deeply repulsive.

grounded_facts: Dr Chapman publicly questions the stability of Dr Jaffe's surgical method, implying it is temporary and flawed.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Dr Chapman publicly challenge Dr Jaffe's technique, saying it was unstable and would make the patient look like 'Grandma Moses' in six months.

grounded_facts: A high-society gathering hosted by Sam's mother in her lavishly appointed flat, attended by Central Service elites and associates.
memories.memory_text: I realized I was at one of my mother's high-society gatherings filled with Central Service elites when I saw Dr Chapman arrive and later noticed someone pushing through the party guests.

grounded_facts: Mrs Terrain informs Sam of a surgical complication, indicating ongoing physical vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Mrs Terrain that there was a slight complication from her surgery, though she insisted it was nothing to worry about.

grounded_facts: Mrs Terrain forcibly brings Sam to meet her daughter Shirley, facilitating an awkward encounter.
memories.memory_text: I tried to disengage, but Mrs Terrain grabbed me and dragged me through the party to meet her daughter Shirley, making the whole encounter feel forced and awkward.

grounded_facts: Sam attempts to clarify he has no romantic interest in Shirley, who responds that she doesn't like him either.
memories.memory_text: I tried to tell Shirley I wasn't interested in her romantically by saying I wanted to meet someone else, and she quickly responded that she didn't like me either, which ended the whole awkward exchange.

grounded_facts: Jack proudly tells Sam that Alison had ear surgery by Dr Jaffe, despite her discomfort with the revelation.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Jack that Alison had her ears pinned back by Dr Jaffe, and I could see she wasn't comfortable with him saying it.

grounded_facts: Mr Helpmann incorrectly calls Alison 'Barbara', forcing Jack to signal her to accept the error.
memories.memory_text: I saw Mr Helpmann call Alison 'Barbara', and I noticed Jack signal her not to correct him, so she stayed silent even though it was wrong.

grounded_facts: Mr Helpmann approaches Sam privately and states he needs his assistance, initiating a pivotal interaction.
memories.memory_text: I was called by Mr Helpmann, and he told me, 'I need your help, Sam,' which made me realize he was turning to me for something important.

grounded_facts: Sam accidentally knocks over a pot, spilling powder onto the wash-stand, creating the surface Helpmann later uses to trace letters.
memories.memory_text: I accidentally knocked over a pot while moving Mr Helpmann, spilling powder across the wash-stand.

grounded_facts: Helpmann offers Sam a position on the Information Retrieval team, referencing a promise to Sam's mother.
Helpmann discloses that he promised Sam's mother to take him onto the Information Retrieval team, providing emotional and institutional weight to the offer.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Helpmann that he promised my mother he'd take me onto the Information Retrieval team, and that's why he was offering me the position.

grounded_facts: Sam reverses his previous stance and asks to accept the transfer to Information Retrieval.
Sam decides to accept the job transfer to Information Retrieval after initially hesitating, reversing his prior decision.
memories.memory_text: I changed my mind and asked Helpmann if I could still accept the transfer to Information Retrieval, wondering if it was too late.

grounded_facts: Helpmann formally welcomes Sam to Information Retrieval by shaking his hand.
memories.memory_text: I remember Helpmann putting out his hand and me taking it, and he said, 'Welcome to Information Retrieval!'—it felt like I was finally being accepted onto the team.

grounded_facts: A private conversation between Sam and Mr Helpmann in MOTHER's bathroom after Helpmann uses the lavatory, during which key personal and professional matters are discussed.
memories.memory_text: I helped Mr Helpmann after he used the lavatory, and during our conversation, he told me he had promised my mother to get me onto the Information Retrieval team; I told him I wanted to accept the transfer, and he welcomed me with a handshake.

grounded_facts: After Sam accepts the transfer, Helpmann blows away the spilled powder and the traced letters EREIAMJH, symbolizing closure and transition.
memories.memory_text: After I accepted the transfer, I saw Helpmann trace the letters EREIAMJH in the powder I had spilled, and then he blew it all away, as if closing a chapter.

grounded_facts: Helpmann traces the anagram 'EREIAMJH' in the spilled powder on the wash-stand, referencing the ghost of Sam's father Jeremiah.
memories.memory_text: I saw Mr Helpmann trace the letters 'EREIAMJH' in the powder I had spilled on the wash-stand, and he said it was like his ghost speaking—'Here I am, J.H.'—but then he blew the powder away.

grounded_facts: Sam enters the austere lobby of Information Retrieval and approaches the reception desk.
memories.memory_text: I entered the austere lobby of Information Retrieval and approached the reception desk.

grounded_facts: A formal but minimal check-in procedure at the Information Retrieval department where Sam reports for duty.
memories.memory_text: I reported to the porter, telling him my name and that I had to report to Mr Warren, and he handed me an ID badge without checking anything.

grounded_facts: Despite offering his ID and expecting a security check, Sam is allowed entry without any verification by the porter.
The porter confidently tells Sam that no search or ID check is necessary, emphasizing the exclusivity of the department.
memories.memory_text: I offered my ID cards and asked if he wanted to search me, but the porter told me no check was necessary, saying I couldn't be just anybody because this was Information Retrieval.

grounded_facts: Multiple expediters simultaneously attempt to gain Mr Warren's attention with documents and urgent requests.
memories.memory_text: I saw multiple expediters rushing around Mr Warren, all trying to get his attention at once with papers and urgent requests, and the whole group was moving fast toward me.

grounded_facts: A moving group of expediters surrounding Mr Warren arrives and passes Sam in the corridor, creating a moment of intense activity before silence returns.
An informal, mobile gathering of expediters clustered around Mr Warren as he moves through the corridor, making rapid decisions while being bombarded with requests.
memories.memory_text: I stepped out of the lift and heard nothing at first, but then a fast-moving group of expediters surrounded Mr Warren came rushing down the corridor, papers and questions flying, making quick decisions as people dropped in and out—I didn’t have the nerve to jump into that chaos.

grounded_facts: After the group passes, Sam decides to follow the scrum down the corridor.
memories.memory_text: I decided to follow the scrum down the corridor after they passed me.

grounded_facts: Warren suddenly pivots, swinging Sam around to face the door of his new office.
memories.memory_text: I felt suddenly swung around when Warren pivoted and turned me to face the door of my new office.

grounded_facts: Mr. Warren acknowledges Sam, gives him a rushed welcome, and assigns him to office DZ/015 with ceremonial emphasis.
Sam is officially given his own office with the designation DZ/015 by Mr. Warren during a hurried corridor encounter.
memories.memory_text: I remember Mr. Warren acknowledging me, giving me a rushed welcome, and officially assigning me to office DZ/015 with ceremonial emphasis, saying, 'Congratulations, DZ/015, welcome to the team.'

grounded_facts: A mobile, informal onboarding event led by Mr. Warren as he moves through the corridor, assigning Sam to his office.
memories.memory_text: I was involved in a mobile, informal onboarding with Mr. Warren as he moved through the corridor, assigning me to my new office.

grounded_facts: Sam enters his new office and observes its cramped, poorly constructed state, indicating low status or systemic dysfunction.
memories.memory_text: I entered my new office and saw how cramped and poorly put together it was—only about four feet wide, with a wall cutting through the desk and a blacked-out window high up. I realized this was nothing like the official assignment suggested.

grounded_facts: Sam tries to pull the desk back from the wall but fails despite strong effort.
memories.memory_text: I tried to pull my desk back from the wall, really strained and gritted my teeth, but it just wouldn't budge no matter how hard I pulled.

grounded_facts: Sam's desk begins to sink into the wall, causing his phone books to fall over repeatedly.
memories.memory_text: I was arranging things at my desk when I noticed the phone books I'd placed against the wall kept falling over whenever I looked away, and then, right before my eyes, my desk started sinking into the wall—I tried pulling it back, but it wouldn't budge, so I gave up and headed for the door.

grounded_facts: After failing to free the desk, Sam gets up, walks around it, and heads for the door.
memories.memory_text: I got up after failing to pull my desk back from the wall, walked around it, and headed for the door.

grounded_facts: Sam visits Lime's office during the day to request use of a computer console.
memories.memory_text: I walked to Lime's office during the day and saw that his workspace was similar to mine, though he was focused on adjusting the desk and didn't notice me at first.

grounded_facts: Sam asks Harvey Lime to borrow his computer console to check information about Jill.
memories.memory_text: I asked Harvey Lime if I could borrow his computer console to check some information about Jill.

grounded_facts: Lime responds to Sam's inquiry about a woman with suggestive leering and insinuation.
memories.memory_text: I asked Lime about a woman, and he responded by leering at me, saying 'A woman eh? I see,' and then later, still leering, asked if she was my dream girl.

grounded_facts: Lime initially mistakes Sam for someone trying to take chairs and responds irritably.
memories.memory_text: I approached Lime to use his console, but he snapped at me, thinking I was trying to take his chairs, and demanded to know who I was.

grounded_facts: Lime takes the print-out from Sam and offers to run the search himself after refusing to lend the console.
memories.memory_text: I handed my print-out to Lime so he could run the search for me, but he took it and started punching the keys himself, even though I had asked to use the console.

grounded_facts: Lime fails to operate the console until Sam points out it is not switched on.
memories.memory_text: I saw Lime struggling with the console and heard him say it was broken, so I pointed out to him that he hadn't switched it on.

grounded_facts: Lime tells Sam to leave, claiming he is distracted by his presence.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Lime to leave his office because I was putting him off, so I went back to my own office to wait for him to finish.

grounded_facts: Sam exits Lime's office after being told to return to his own and wait.
memories.memory_text: I hesitated but then left Lime's office after he told me to go back to my own and wait.

grounded_facts: Sam arrives at a massive stone ship floating on the icy sea, using his new wings to approach and land on it.
memories.memory_text: I used my new wings to fly over the icy sea and landed on the massive stone ship.

grounded_facts: Sam finds a loose stone forming a ledge, jumps onto it, and squeezes through a gap into a dark passage within the stone ship.
memories.memory_text: I found a loose stone ledge, jumped onto it, and squeezed through a gap into a dark passage inside the ship.

grounded_facts: Sam's exploration of the mysterious stone ship, including his arrival, entry, and initial discoveries within.
memories.memory_text: I explored the stone ship, arriving on it with my wings, entering through a narrow gap, and seeing an enormous abyss and a glimpse of sky before hearing a distant moan.

grounded_facts: After entering the ship, Sam sees a vast inner abyss where hundreds of grey-shrouded prisoners are huddled at the bottom.
memories.memory_text: I emerged from an opening and found myself teetering over a huge abyss, where far below I saw hundreds of grey-shrouded prisoners huddled at the bottom.

grounded_facts: A series of loud booms echo through the stone ship, causing it to tremble and forcing Sam to steady himself.
memories.memory_text: I heard a great boom echo through the ship and didn't know where it came from; the noise made the ship tremble, and I had to steady myself as another boom hit and I clutched at the wall.

grounded_facts: Sam observes the desk moving further into Lime's office through the wall.
memories.memory_text: I looked back as I was leaving my office and saw my desk creeping further through the wall into Lime's office.

grounded_facts: Sam uses Lime's computer without permission, ignoring Lime's protest, asserting control over the investigative process.
memories.memory_text: I sat at Lime's desk and started using his computer, and even though he protested and said it was his desk, I went ahead anyway.

grounded_facts: Sam uses Lime's computer to retrieve detailed information about Gillian Layton, identifying her as a suspect with a specific code and occupation, which was not previously known to him.
A focused inquiry by Sam to uncover classified details about Gillian Layton's identity and status, conducted through computer access in Lime's office.
memories.memory_text: I used Lime's computer to pull up classified details about Gillian Layton and found out she's Suspect S/5173, a truck driver, with more information logged under reference officer 412/L in Room 5001.

grounded_facts: Warren issues a series of overlapping instructions to Sam, mixing personnel, logistics, and appearance-related comments.
Warren delegates multiple administrative tasks to Sam, including handling paperwork, arranging a conference, and resolving a transportation query.
memories.memory_text: I was given a string of overlapping instructions by Warren as we moved through the corridor—he told me to handle paperwork, arrange a conference, sort out a transportation query, and even get a new suit, all while mixing personnel and logistics comments.

grounded_facts: Sam boards an elevator that already contains a charlady with cleaning supplies, marking a shift in location and social context.
memories.memory_text: I stepped into an awaiting lift to disengage, and I noticed a charlady already inside with her cleaning supplies, which shifted the whole tone from tense directive to quiet, shared space.

grounded_facts: Sam hears a man screaming in pain from afar and reacts with concern, noticing an air conditioning vent in the ceiling of the lift.
memories.memory_text: I heard a man screaming in pain from somewhere far away, and I looked around the lift, noticing the air conditioning vent in the ceiling.

grounded_facts: Sam asks the charlady if the screams disturb her, seeking confirmation of shared awareness.
memories.memory_text: I asked the charlady what that sound was and whether it didn't disturb her, because I wanted to know if she was aware of it too.

grounded_facts: The charlady removes wax earplugs, indicating her deliberate disengagement from the environment and the screams.
memories.memory_text: I saw the charlady pull out wax earplugs from her ears after I asked about the screams, and she just smiled at me.

grounded_facts: Sam reaches the door marked 5001 after walking down the corridor from the elevator.
memories.memory_text: I walked down the clean, white-tiled corridor from the elevator, passed a technician in a white coat, and reached the door marked 5001.

grounded_facts: Following the light change, Sam enters the room.
memories.memory_text: After the light turned green, I entered the room.

grounded_facts: After Sam knocks, the red light above door 5001 turns off and the green light turns on, indicating access is granted.
memories.memory_text: I knocked on the door of room 5001, and I saw the red light go off and the green light come on, which I knew meant I was allowed in.

grounded_facts: Sam enters Room 500l and waits near the typist, indicating he is seeking someone or something specific.
memories.memory_text: I entered Room 500l and waited near the typist, looking around for Officer 412/L since that's who I needed to find.

grounded_facts: The typist silently greets Sam with a twinkling gesture while continuing to type.
memories.memory_text: I saw the typist twinkling a greeting at me while she kept typing, silently letting me know she acknowledged me and that help was on the way.

grounded_facts: Sam sees and reacts to the violent and distressed content being typed, showing discomfort or recognition.
memories.memory_text: I saw the violent words being typed and felt a jolt—something in the text made me wince, like I recognized it or felt it too deeply.

grounded_facts: The typist pauses briefly to ask if she can help Sam, showing attentiveness despite being occupied.
memories.memory_text: I was still processing what I'd read when the typist paused and asked if she could help me, as if she noticed I was unsettled.

grounded_facts: Sam states he is looking for Officer 412/L, indicating a goal to locate this individual.
memories.memory_text: I told the typist I'm looking for Officer 412/L.

grounded_facts: A recorded audio session involving distressing content is transcribed by the typist in real time.
memories.memory_text: I heard a recorded voice screaming in distress—'AHHHH, Oh God ... No, don't ... STOP!!' and later 'Oooooooh ... aaaaaahhh ... please ...'—while the typist transcribed it live, and I knew it was real when she muttered, 'I thought so!' as she finished.

grounded_facts: The typist stops typing upon realizing the session is over, removes her earphones, and begins organizing the copies.
memories.memory_text: I saw the typist stop typing, take off her earphones, and start organizing the copies from the typewriter.

grounded_facts: After the figure exits and the technician leaves, the typist signals that Sam may now enter the inner area.
memories.memory_text: After I saw a figure wave and exit through the frosted glass door and a technician leave to the left, I watched the typist signal that I could go into the inner area.

grounded_facts: The typist informs Sam that he may now enter the inner area.
memories.memory_text: I was told by the typist that I could go in now.

grounded_facts: Sam enters Jack Lint's office and confirms his identity, initiating a conversation about a security-level inquiry.

memories.memory_text: I saw a young man step in to protect my mother, and he challenged me aggressively when I approached, asking if I was bothering her.

grounded_facts: A squad of troops bursts into the chapel, causing panic and scattering the mourners.
memories.memory_text: I saw a squad of troops burst into the chapel, and I panicked as people started screaming and scattering all around me.

grounded_facts: During a chaotic troop invasion, Sam crashes into the coffin, causing it to fall and spill its contents — a large quantity of offal.
memories.memory_text: I crashed into the coffin while trying to escape, and I saw it spill a huge pile of offal instead of a body.

grounded_facts: Sam reaches a dead end in the maze, blocked by a pile of consumer waste with no visible escape route.
memories.memory_text: I kept turning corners, hoping for a way out, but then I found myself at a dead end with no path forward—just a massive pile of broken TVs, washing machines, and junk blocking my escape, and I realized I'd have to try digging through it.

grounded_facts: Sam discovers a hidden door in the wall behind the pile of junk, which he opens and escapes through.
memories.memory_text: I was backed against the wall with no way out, so I started digging through the junk, and as I pressed against the wall, I felt a door knob; I turned it, the door opened, and I dove through to escape.

grounded_facts: Sam enters a sparsely furnished room and attempts to secure the door from pursuit.
memories.memory_text: I entered a nearly empty room and tried to lock the door behind me, but there was no key, so I braced it with my weight to keep it shut before finally letting go carefully.

grounded_facts: Sam opens the door slightly and sees the outside environment moving away.
memories.memory_text: I carefully opened the door a crack and saw the street receding from my point of view, confirming the outside was moving away.

grounded_facts: Sam observes through the window that Jill is driving the cab, recognizing her face in the mirror after seeing the driver wearing her cap.
Jill raises her head to reveal her face in the driving mirror and smiles at Sam after he bangs on the cab window.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jill's cab, and when I noticed the driver was wearing her cap, I banged on the window; then I saw her face in the mirror and she smiled at me, confirming it was really her.

grounded_facts: After recognizing Jill, Sam breaks down in sobs of relief and love.
memories.memory_text: I broke down in sobs of relief and love when I recognized Jill in the mirror and saw her smile.

grounded_facts: JILL and SAM exchange a brief glance while driving at dawn, indicating shared awareness or unspoken communication.
memories.memory_text: I exchanged a brief glance with Jill while we were driving at dawn, and in that moment, I felt a shared awareness between us.

grounded_facts: Jill greets Sam in the morning as she enters the room, initiating their daily interaction.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jill entering the room and greeting me in the morning, starting our day together.

grounded_facts: Jill asks Sam if he slept well, initiating morning interaction.
memories.memory_text: I recall Jill asking me if I slept well, her voice coming from off screen as she checked in on me.

grounded_facts: Sam reveals that he no longer dreams, sharing a personal change with Jill.
memories.memory_text: I told Jill that I don't dream anymore, sharing something personal about how I've changed.

grounded_facts: Sam states that he no longer dreams, indicating a change in his psychological or neurological state.
memories.memory_text: I realized I no longer dream, and I spoke it aloud to Jill, acknowledging a shift in my inner life.

grounded_facts: Sam physically embraces Jill upon her entry, signaling emotional connection or need.
memories.memory_text: I embraced Jill after speaking, holding her close as a way to connect and seek comfort.

grounded_facts: Sam mentally and physically disconnects from the Information Retrieval Room, symbolically ascending into a transcendent sky as he hums the song 'Brazil'.
memories.memory_text: I sat in the chair, still strapped in, but I could feel myself floating away as I hummed 'Brazil'—the room fell away and I rose into a glorious sky, the music swelling around me like it was always meant to carry me home.

memories.memory_text: I was in the bath, just trying to clean off the day, watching Bilko in the mirror—then suddenly a man in uniform blocked the screen, and I couldn't see his face, just his body looming there. I froze, heart pounding, and all I could get out was 'Who's there?'
I saw Sam burst out and run toward the burning car, then I came roaring around the corner in the lorry—he spotted me and started chasing after it, shouting something desperate.
Later, I heard that the girl—Buttle’s daughter—told Sam my name, though I wasn’t there when it happened.
They know my name, my face, my body—I can feel it spreading, like ink in water. If they’ve reached the records, they’ve seen everything: the scar, the blemish, the weight of me reduced to numbers.
I stood at the porter's desk demanding he re-stamp my form—he'd done it before, so why not now? His refusal made my skin crawl, like the system was tightening around me again.
I slammed my fist on the desk and told Porter those weren't tits—he was looking at twenty pounds of high explosive, and I'd blow the place up if he didn't stamp the form.

I was just standing there with the form when suddenly armed guards burst out of secret doors, shouting 'DROP IT!!'—I dropped it right away, hands up, heart pounding. I couldn't believe they were treating me like a threat.

Sam rushed in and shouted 'STOP! Let her go!'—then the guards snapped to attention when they saw his badge. I didn't understand what was happening, but he grabbed me and pulled me away, saying it was a classified matter.
I was already pulling away in the lorry when I saw Sam sprinting toward me, jumping onto the running board—he barely made it inside.
I stared at him, engine off, and demanded to know who he was—no way was I driving blind with some panicked man babbling about dreams and danger.
After he dropped papers all over my cab, I told him straight—'Don't litter my cab!'—and watched him scramble to pick them up like he finally remembered I was in charge here.
I told Sam to shut up about his dreams—I don’t care what he thinks or feels. It’s my life, not his.
I asked Sam where he was taking me, then realized—no, I’m the one driving. I’m in control now.
I told Sam not to act guilty, to act like me—just doing the job—because I could see he was poking around, getting too curious for his own good.
When the lorry stopped, I reached behind the seat and took the package, quickly slipping it under my jacket while checking that Sam wasn’t looking.
I moved toward the corner of the metal structure, keeping low, scanning for watchers—there was no time to hesitate, not with the parcel burning a hole in my hands.
We passed the parcels—mine to them, theirs to me—fast, no words, just a shift of weight and a glance toward the Ministry poster that felt like it was watching us.
I turned the key and felt the engine roar to life under my hands, the parcel wedged behind me like a silent passenger, Sam’s eyes burning into my neck as we pulled away.

I told him it was a Christmas present, and when he picked it up and gave me that look, I just said, 'Open it if you don't trust me,' like I didn't care—but I watched him, waiting to see if he'd actually do it.
I pushed Sam on what Information Retrieval really does, how it claims to fight terrorists but ends up destroying innocent lives like the Buttles'.
I threw out that line about wars having innocent victims, then hit him with 'Who is this war against, Sam?'—watching him fumble for an answer that wasn’t there.
I saw the clock as we passed it—right on time, just like always. I said it out loud, maybe to steady myself, knowing I had to punch in by five.
Sam lunged for the wheel—I shoved him back, but he kept grabbing, trying to force a turn. I couldn't control the lorry while he was tearing at the steering wheel, screaming at me to stop.
I was fighting Sam for control of the lorry, screaming that he was mad, completely out of his mind—then the sirens ripped through the air and we both turned to look.
I grabbed for control of the lorry, shouting at Sam to stop—we can't outrun them, he's going to get us killed.
I shouted at Sam not to touch the gear levers while we were fighting for control of the lorry, the security vehicles closing in behind us.
I felt Sam shove my hand away and then that awful jolt when the trailer ripped loose from the cab—I knew right then we were in real trouble.
I snapped at Sam, 'We? Don't blame me!'—I couldn't let him pin this on us like we were in it together.
I saw the house burning behind us and shouted 'Shit! The house is on fire!'—then I had to snap Sam out of it, tapping his forehead, telling him to come back.
Sam grabbed the parcel from the trolley like he had any right to it—like he didn’t already ruin everything. I lunged for it, heart slamming, because that thing wasn’t his to touch.
Sam grabbed the parcel I was carrying—the one from the power plant. I didn’t throw it at him. We were in the lingerie department when he started questioning me, then lunged for it.
I asked Dowser if he repeats everything, and he just nodded, confirming it like it was nothing—his voice flat, echoing Spoor’s words like a broken machine.
The porter looked me up and down and asked if I was a professional—like I was some kind of threat or fraud—and I just said, 'No, amateur,' like it was obvious.

relations.relation_summary: The relationship between Jill Layton and Sam Lowry is defined by a complex interplay of romantic passion, mutual survival efforts, and recurring conflict. Social relationship evidence reveals a deep romantic connection, beginning with Sam's idealization of Jill as his 'Dream Girl,' which evolves into a tangible emotional bond marked by physical intimacy, declarations of love, and protective behaviors. Their romantic involvement is evident in multiple shared moments: passionate kisses, embraces, and Sam’s explicit statement, 'I love you,' as well as Jill’s reciprocal affection and concern for his safety. This emotional core drives Sam to falsify records to save Jill and pursue her after her disappearance, demonstrating his profound personal investment. Concurrently, they function as collaborators in resistance against a repressive system, jointly evading government persecution, discussing systemic flaws with shared laughter, and coordinating escape attempts. Key events such as fleeing together, struggling for control of the lorry, and warning each other of danger underscore their cooperative dynamic under pressure. However, their relationship is also marked by significant hostility and tension. They engage in physical struggles over vehicle control, exchange accusations (Jill calling Sam 'mad,' Sam blaming Jill for failures), and experience moments of distrust and confrontation, particularly during high-stress situations. These conflicts reveal a power struggle and divergent risk assessments, yet are consistently followed by reconciliation or renewed cooperation. Despite antagonistic episodes, both characters repeatedly demonstrate concern for the other’s safety—Sam urging Jill to avoid danger, Jill intervening to stop reckless actions—indicating a resilient emotional support system. The relationship evolves from initial tension and suspicion into a deeply entangled bond of love, dependency, and shared resistance, ultimately shaping both characters’ decisions and actions throughout the narrative. The push-pull between affection and conflict reflects the broader thematic struggle between individual desire and systemic oppression.

memories.memory_text: I cut them down—one after another—the robed figures falling like shadows under my blade, their bodies piling up in a heap of black cloth while I barely got a scratch.
The pile of black shapes began to rise, turning into a churning cloud of flapping cloth. It lifted off the ground and flew away, emitting a terrifying maniacal laughter.
I had her—she was right there in the cage, and I told her she was safe, that no one could ever reach us up on that platform surrounded by all those eyes watching the sky.

The sky started cracking like glass, then whole blocks of it were ripped out, one by one, until everything went black—and then I saw that flapping black shape coming at me, and I couldn’t move fast enough.

I saw the cheque Kurtzman handed me and realized it was meant for Tuttle—but he’d already panicked, correcting himself, saying it was Buttle. I could feel the weight of it, like it was something dangerous just to hold.
I sat at the console and started checking the system—Buttle was flagged everywhere as gone: dormanted, deleted, inoperative. I remember thinking, he’s not just missing—he’s been erased.
I burst into Jill's flat and saw a hole in the floor—everything looked abandoned, like she’d been ripped out of here suddenly.
I heard an explosion, ran to the window, and saw my car on fire—Jill was running across the forecourt with a suitcase and bundles, getting away fast.
I punched in Gillian Layton’s name and pulled up her file—Suspect S/5173, truck driver, all inquiries to Room 5001. That’s what I needed.
I was running full speed toward the lorry as it started moving, and I barely managed to leap onto the running board and haul myself up into the cab.

I found the luggage Jill had taken from the apartment hidden behind the seats in the lorry—same pieces she carried away, now crammed in with rags and grease. My sleeve got dirty when I opened the compartment, and I was still checking them when the door suddenly flew open.

I saw her pull a package from behind the seat, look around quickly, and slide it under her jacket before walking off. I didn’t see what it was—just the way she moved, furtive, like she didn’t want me to know.
I begged Jack to help me check if Jill had been arrested, but he shut me down, saying she was involved in blowing up security men and linked to Tuttle’s sabotage—then just left me standing there.
I remember stepping out of the lift with Jack, desperate to make him understand—Jill was innocent—but instead of helping, he just asked me to stay away from him.

I walked in and my breath turned to steam—everything was torn open, frozen, like my apartment had been gutted and left to die. When I asked what happened, they just said 'Thermostat's gone. And then some,' like that explained the wreckage.

I told Jill I’d be back soon and not to answer the phone or the door—she looked worried, and when she said 'Don’t do anything silly,' I could hear the fear in her voice, but I had to go. I’m going to pull some strings at the Ministry, even if it’s dangerous, because it’s the only way to fix this mess and keep her safe.
I saw my mother's picture sitting on Helpmann's desk—just there, out in the open, like it was normal. I didn't understand why it was in his office, of all places.
The machine printed that Trollope was dead—'resisting arrest'—but no arrest was ever logged. I watched the message come through twice, and then I turned the system back on. Something was very wrong.
I opened the door and saw her—dancing in that glowing light, wearing my mother’s wig, floating like the girl from my dreams. I couldn’t speak. It was her, but it couldn’t be.
She looked at me after reading the print-out and said, 'Care for a bit of necrophilia?'—and then we rushed together. I don’t know if it was real, but I felt it.
I soared up into that brilliant blue sky, my wings catching the light—I could see the clouds rushing, and for the first moment, I knew I had found the day.
I drove my sword into the column with everything I had—the crack split upward, and when the cube shattered, the sky burst free and the prisoners' chains fell away.

I woke up and saw the light on the wall, and for a moment I smiled—I remembered where I was, and I reached for Jill. She wasn't there, and I panicked—then she said 'Merry Xmas' and crawled back to me. I held her and said, 'Everything is going to be all right.'

There was a crash—something tore through the ceiling like a drill. Guards slid down a pole, grabbed me, called me 'Turncoat Bastard' and 'Traitor.' A bag was pulled over my head, and just before everything went black, I heard a shot and Jill screamed.
I screamed for Jack, begging him to stop—he was coming at me with that thing, mask half off, shouting it was a professional relationship, but his voice was breaking like he didn’t believe it either.

The ceiling exploded open and Tuttle dropped through with armed men behind him—guns firing, Jack falling, then the room shaking from an explosion right after Tuttle yelled 'Detonate!' and started unstrapping me.
I was running down those endless stairs, fighting, bleeding, shots ringing out all around me—I don’t even know who was left, just that I had to keep moving.
Tuttle threw me a dark overcoat, and I pulled it on fast to hide my light grey detainee clothes.
We burst through the door together, running into the open forecourt while gunfire echoed behind us.
I saw the building explode—huge bursts of fire and debris everywhere, and all those files just tearing out into the sky like snow, fluttering down over everything.
I turned to find Tuttle after the blast, but he was gone—completely gone—and then I heard gunfire closing in, so I ran.
I burst into the flat and ran straight to the bedroom—everything was gone, just empty walls and curtains blowing in the wind. I couldn’t find any sign she’d ever been there.
I was trapped at the end of the maze, digging through that pile of broken machines—televisions, washers, junk everywhere—just trying to find something to defend myself as the agents closed in.
My hand brushed against a door knob as I pressed against the wall—turned it, and the door just opened. I didn't think, I just dove through.
I saw the driver’s head in the mirror, wearing Jill’s cap, and when she looked up and smiled, I knew it was her—alive, real, here for me. I couldn’t hold it back, I just sobbed.
I woke up and saw her come through the door, and when she asked if I slept well, I just nodded and said it quietly—'I don't dream anymore'—before pulling her close.

I'm sitting in the chair, strapped in, but I can't feel the restraints anymore—just the warmth of the sky opening up around me, and my humming rising into something grander, like an orchestra answering me.
I see Helpmann and someone else turn away, their backs receding—Jack said 'He's gone'—and I know they think I'm lost, but I'm not gone, I'm finally here, finally free, singing into the sky.
